artworks.title: Plate 1: Pedro González (Petrus Gonsalvus) and His Wife, Catherine
artworks.medium: watercolor and gold paint on parchment
artworks.dimensions: page size (approximate): 14.3 x 18.4 cm (5 5/8 x 7 1/4 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Lessing J. Rosenwald
artworks.description: Set within a drawn oval frame, two people are shown from the waist up against a parchment-white background in this horizontal watercolor portrait. To the left, the man’s face is entirely covered with golden brown hair, leaving space for only the eyes, the protruding nose, and mouth. He looks at us, wearing a narrow white collar over a lapis-blue robe with black sleeves. To our right, a woman rests one hand on his near shoulder. Her body is angled toward him, to the left, and she looks off in that direction. She has a round face, pale skin, rosy cheeks, and dark pink lips. She wears a black cap with a wide, flat strip of cloth draped from front to back. Her black dress has a white ruff collar, puffed sleeves, a cinched waist, and a full skirt. The pair stand behind what appears to be a grassy ledge with a twig growing out of a rise to the left. The background behind them and beyond the gold line border is white. Latin text is handwritten above and below the gold oval frame in two colors of ink. Above and in purple, text reads, “Omni miraculo quod fit per Hominem maius miraculum est Homo visibilium omnium maximus est Mundus, invisibilium DEVS sed mundum esse cospicimus,  Deum esse Credimus…” Below and in yellow ink, text reads, ““HOMO natus de MVLIERE, brevi viventis Tempore Repletus multis miseriis. Job 14.”

Near the top right, another butterfly or moth is positioned with open wings, and in the bottom right, an insect with transparent wings and a dark body is illustrated. The colors in the image are primarily earthy browns, soft grays, and muted greens, with subtle touches of pink on the berries adding a hint of brightness. The position of the subjects in the illustration is deliberate, with each insect numbered and spaced around the central branch, creating a harmonious circular composition.

artworks.title: Plate 2: Maddalena and Enrico, the Children of Pedro González (Petrus Gonsalvus)
artworks.medium: watercolor and gold paint on parchment
artworks.dimensions: page size (approximate): 14.3 x 18.4 cm (5 5/8 x 7 1/4 in.)

artworks.description: This painting depicts two children standing upright, wearing elaborate garments. They face slightly to the right and look off in that direction. The children appear to have pale skin, but their faces are both covered in short brown fur or hair. Their eyes, noses, and mouths are still visible. The taller child on the left wears an embellished pink gown with a ruffled lace collar, puffy white sleeves, a bejeweled neckline, and a large cross pendant with jewels hanging from it. This child appears to have long hair on their head that is braided to look like a tiara, and the top of their head is covered with colorful jewels. The shorter child on the right stands with their hand resting on a rock on the right edge of the painting. They wear a bright pink gown with a ruffled lace collar and embroidery down the front and on the shoulders. They wear a tall pink hat. The ground beneath these two children is a light brown color with some small rocks, and behind them is plain paper. These figures are encircled in a gold oval frame with Latin text above and below it.
